content: Individuals diagnosed with diabetes are at an increased risk of developing heart failure, even if they do not exhibit any symptoms. Scientific studies have demonstrated that diabetes is associated with a higher prevalence of structural abnormalities in the heart, which may predispose individuals to heart failure. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) recommends enhanced screening protocols for patients with diabetes who are considered to be at high risk for heart failure. Specific biomarkers, such as N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), have proven to be effective in identifying these high-risk individuals at an earlier stage. Research indicates that proactive monitoring for the development of heart failure in these patients can lead to significant benefits, including a reduction in the risk of hospitalizations and mortality rates.
